requirements.summary: DNS capture shows zero browser-originated DNS; packet capture shows zero ordinary networking
requirements.note: measured 2026-09-01 (Nomad-browser f96e650, capture_test.go): the client loads and searches the corpus inside a network namespace with loopback up, and the packets that namespace's interfaces carried come to zero, against a control run carrying 64 in the same namespace. DNS included, since a DNS query is a packet. A tcpdump capture was tried first and abandoned: in a user namespace it reported '48 packets received by filter, 0 packets captured' on roughly two runs in three, and every one of those zeros is indistinguishable from this criterion's own claim. /proc/net/dev has no attach to race and needs no privilege. Three controls: all three namespace mechanisms carry 64; a client made to emit is caught; a counter stubbed to zero is caught by the control. PARTIAL rather than VERIFIED because it measures the Go client on Linux only -- the macOS client and the engine forks are not covered, and per DEC-013 the forks are parked.

requirements.summary: authenticated updater, anti-rollback, fail closed, recovery; architecturally unable to grant the networkless browser web capability (separate constrained component); update-check cadence private-state-independent
requirements.note: Nomad-browser/update verifies a release the user already has and downloads nothing: an updater that fetches is a network client inside the binary that is supposed to have none, so the division is enforced by a dependency test rather than intended. Rollback (including a pre-release of the installed version), equivocation (two signed artefacts for one version, refused rather than resolved) and substitution are each refused by name. Fails closed throughout: unknown manifest version refused rather than downgraded, untrusted signer refused although internally consistent, unreadable watermark refuses the install rather than being read as absent. cmd/nomad-browser-verify has no compiled-in release key and says so (EB-7). No installer integration, so this is a manual step (Nomad-browser 9121eca) The verifier binary itself is now tested: run and trustedKeys were at zero coverage while the update package under them was well covered, and the untested branch -- a build with no compiled-in release key refusing rather than proceeding with an empty trust set -- is the one every current build takes. Anti-rollback and dry-run are asserted end to end through the binary, three mutations killed. EVIDENCE_INDEX F-20.

requirements.summary: OS-backed key storage (Keychain), no plaintext secrets
requirements.note: the client-side plaintext secret is closed and the OS-backed half is not. publish.Options.Key is a required KeySource with no default: Passphrase derives the queue key with Argon2id from a passphrase and a per-queue salt, leaving nothing on the disk that opens the queue, and UnprotectedKeyFile is the previous co-located key file named for what it is. Both directions are measured -- every file in a passphrase queue tried as the key opens nothing, and the unprotected key file does open a fragment -- and a wrong passphrase fails at Open rather than surfacing as an empty queue. The passphrase reaches cmd/nomad-publish on a file descriptor, not argv or the environment. EVIDENCE_INDEX F-12. Still missing: Keychain or an equivalent OS keystore, and the operator-side secrets (threshold shares, operator identity, authority key) remain plaintext files at 0600. The trusted release public key is a build constant, which is where a public key belongs; its private half still has no documented custody. The operator-side file boundary is now tested rather than merely implemented: the permission, regular-file and size checks on the operator secrets, the authority private key and the threshold share were at zero coverage across the repository and nine mutations over them are now killed, including a check written as an equality that would refuse a 0400 mounted secret. EVIDENCE_INDEX F-16. The secrets themselves are still plaintext files.

requirements.summary: clean uninstall/private-data removal test; OS retention documented
requirements.note: macos/scripts/uninstall.sh removes the sandbox container (which under the sandbox holds every path the app can write) plus unsandboxed development locations, refuses to run while the app is open, and supports --dry-run. docs/DATA_RETENTION.md documents what macOS keeps anyway -- crash reports carrying raw stack words, snapshots, Spotlight, unified log, swap -- with the command for each. uninstall_test.go cross-checks the script against the Swift sources, Info.plist and the document, each verified by introducing the drift it catches. Never executed against a real installed bundle (Nomad-browser 77d632c) The Linux client needs no cleanup script because it writes nothing: TestTheLinuxClientWritesNothingToDisk walks every package it links and fails on any standard-library call that creates or modifies a path, with a control pointing the detector at a package that does write. linux/README.md documents removal on that basis and what the OS keeps regardless. EVIDENCE_INDEX F-22. The macOS half is unchanged, including that its script has never run against a real installed bundle.

requirements.summary: allowlisted log/telemetry schemas; crash dump privacy audit
requirements.note: the browser emits nothing of its own: no os_log, NSLog or print anywhere in the Swift sources, enforced by the scan in bundle_test.go, and egress.Policy refuses telemetry and crash-reporting as named capabilities. The crash-dump privacy question is answered honestly in docs/DATA_RETENTION.md rather than claimed away: macOS writes .ips reports outside the container with thread stacks as raw machine words, the app cannot prevent them, and upload is the user's setting. nomad-testnet's per-field telemetry allowlist has no browser-side equivalent because the browser has no telemetry schema at all

requirements.summary: immutable commit-addressed release evidence
requirements.note: release artifacts are commit-addressed and the CI release job publishes a gated prerelease with packet, DKG, ceremony and process evidence attached. What is missing is immutability that does not depend on this project: the digests live in a GitHub release the same account can delete or replace, so nothing yet pins them somewhere a maintainer cannot rewrite
